newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mixed.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mixed.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Monday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover fell to 2.516 billion yuan from 1.272 billion yuan with the 20-day contract the most actively traded.

Traders said trading was more active than on Friday because of an increase in fund demand from some grain producing provinces. But many big state-run banks continued to cut their trading volumes, they said.

"The summer grain harvest season has seen some increased borrowing today from some short-term financial centres," one local trader said, adding these included centres from Hunan, Sichuan and Shandong provinces.
However, financial centres such as Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing continued to be lenders, local traders said.
This balanced the market somewhat, so increased demand from the inland provinces did not have a sharp upward impact on rates, another trader said.

The withdrawal of banks from the stock market after the government banned them from trading shares had increased money supply on the market, so rates were not likely to rise sharply despite the seasonal demand, traders said.
They said they expected the rates to move in a narrow range in the next few days.
